$comment: Known-compromised npm releases that must never appear in a tracked lockfile.
This is an incident ledger, not a vulnerability scanner. Entries are exact
name@version pairs published by an attacker who held a maintainer's
credentials — not versions with a CVE. A registry unpublish removes the
tarball from npm, but it does not remove a resolved entry from a lockfile
that was committed during the window, and a warm content-addressable store
can still restore one. This check is what makes that state loud.
A package name may be an exact match ('keyv') or a whole scope ('@keyv/*'),
which is how advisories usually describe a scope-wide compromise.

advisories.summary: Trojanized releases in the keyv and cacheable namespaces. A preinstall hook fetched a standalone Bun runtime and ran an obfuscated second stage that harvested cloud, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions OIDC and npm credentials, then republished other packages using the stolen tokens.
